rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols caused people to stray as the occasion of misguidance, though they lack agency, just as worldly life causes people to be deceived.
rows.anchor: أي : الأصنام أضللن كثيرا من الناس ولذلك سألت منك أن تعصمني وبني

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say devils entered idols and spoke through them: one in Abū Jahl’s idol slandered the Prophet, then the idol professed Islam and warned worshippers, so Abū Jahl smashed it and alleged sorcery.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم كان الاضلال منهن لأن الشياطين كانت تدخل أجواف الأصنام وتتكلم كما حكى أن واحدا من الشياطين دخل جوف صنم أبي جهل

rows.speaker: الكمال الخجندي
rows.claim: Kamal Khujandi’s couplet says breaking the idol of pride in the lovers’ religion is better than a hundred acts of worship.
rows.anchor: قال الكمال الخجندي قدس سره :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is partitive: a follower is like a part of Abraham, inseparable from him; likewise, a cheat is not one of the believers because cheating is not their trait.
rows.anchor: من تبعيضية فالكلام على التشبيه أي كبعضي في عدم الانفكاك عني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disobeying Abraham means not following him; it is set against following just as disbelief is set against gratitude by abandoning thanks.
rows.anchor: ومن عصاني أي لم يتبعني فإنه في مقابلة تبعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can forgive and show mercy to the disobedient either from the outset or after repentance.
rows.anchor: قادر على أن تغفر له وترحمه ابتداء وبعد توبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Ashʿarī theology every sin, even shirk, is rationally forgivable because punishment is God’s right, though scripture says He does not forgive shirk.
rows.anchor: وفي دليل على أن كل ذنب فلله تعالى أن يغفره حتى الشرك

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya says Abraham preserves adab by saying who disobeys me, not who disobeys You; forgiving such a sinner displays exceptional generosity.
rows.anchor: في "التأويلات النجمية" قد حفظ الأدب فيما قال ومن عصاني

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A herald beneath the Throne says God pardoned claims owed to Him by Muhammad’s community; they must pardon one another’s remaining claims, then enter Paradise through His mercy.
rows.anchor: في الحديث : "ينادي مناد من تحت العرش يوم القيامة يا أمة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تبعات is the plural of تبعة, a right or claim owed to another.
rows.anchor: والتبعات جمع تبعة بكسر الباء ما اتبع به من الحق

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
rows.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh says mercy is for sinners if reward is for the obedient; though not obedient, he hopes for reward, and as a sinner he hopes for mercy.
rows.anchor: وذكر أن يحيى بن معاذ الرازي رحمه الله قال إلهي إن كان ثوابك للمطيعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accompanying Persian couplet urges the God-knower toward Paradise and calls sinners fitting recipients of divine generosity.
rows.anchor: نصيب ماست بهشت اي خداشناش برو كه مستحق كرامت كنا هكارانند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham uses the plural Our Lord because the prayer concerns his descendants, making appeal to God’s lordship over them more likely to be accepted.
rows.anchor: والجمع لأن الآية متعلقة بذريته فالتعرض لوصف ربوبيته تعالى لهم أدخل في القبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some descendants means Ishmael and those descended from him, whose settlement is included in Abraham’s own settlement.
rows.anchor: إني أسكنت من ذريتي أي بعض ذريتي وهم إسماعيل ومن ولد منه فإن اسكانه متضمن لإسكانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barren valley is Mecca, a rocky place where nothing grows.
rows.anchor: هو وادي مكة فإنها حجرية لا تنبت أي لا يكون فيها شيء من زرع قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like the Quran without crookedness in 39:28, the valley has no cultivation at all and only absence of growth.
rows.anchor: بمعنى لا يوجد فيه اعوجاج وما فيه إلا الاستقامة لا غير

rows.speaker: تفسير الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh’s Tafsīr describes the valley as between two mountains, with neither water nor cultivated land.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير الشيخ لأنها : واد

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Baḥr al-ʿUlūm notes that God had provided the inhabitants with running water by the commentator’s own time.
rows.anchor: وفي بحر العلوم وأما في زماننا فقد رزق الله أهله ماء جاريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is a locative adjunct of I settled; the House is the Kaaba, and its annexation to God is honorific.
rows.anchor: عند بيتك المحرم ظرف لاسكنت كقولك صليت بمكة عند الركن وهو الكعبة والاضافة للتشريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kaaba is sacred because God forbade harm, fighting, hunting, and entry without ihram; the Flood did not overtake it, so it is also called al-ʿAtīq, the freed one.
rows.anchor: وسمى محرما لأنه عظيم الحرمة حرم الله التعرض له بسوء يوم خلق السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya reads the sacred House as the heart, forbidden to house anything except God, invoking the saying that a believer’s heart contains Him.
rows.anchor: في التأويلات النجمية عند بيتك المحرم وهو القلب المحرم أن يكون بيتا لغير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated Our Lord displays full concern for what follows.
rows.anchor: ربنا كرر النداء لإظهار كمال العناية بما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is purposive and attaches to I settled: Abraham settled them in this barren valley only to establish prayer, not for worldly aims; prayer is singled out for its excellence and role in reforming the soul, while Quraysh resisted it from pride.
rows.anchor: ليقيموا الصلوة اللام لام كي متعلقة باسكنت أي ما اسكنتهم بهذا الوادي البلقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afʾida is the plural of fuʾād, meaning hearts, and min is partitive.
rows.anchor: فاجعل أفئدة من الناس جمع فؤاد وهي القلوب ومن للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tahwī means to hurry toward them in longing or fly toward them with love; hawā can mean falling rapidly, rising, or loving, with ilā expressing longing and inclination.
rows.anchor: يقال هوى يهوى من باب ضرب هويا وهويا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people are Ishmael and his descendants, the believers; partitive min limits the hearts drawn, whereas asking for all people would bring Persians, Romans, Turks, and Indians in a crowd.
rows.anchor: أي : إسماعيل وذريته وهم المؤمنون ولو قال أفئدة الناس بدون من التبعيضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed Persian couplet says one whose beauty lawfully steals the heart is worthy of love, while failing to love such beauty is a burden.
rows.anchor: وآنكس كه براننان جمالى عاشق نشود وبال باشد

rows.speaker: المولى الجامي
rows.claim: Mullā Jāmī’s poem depicts the sanctuary as the beloved’s gracious precinct and the qibla of beauties, drawing admirers toward it.
rows.anchor: قال المولى الجامي قدس سره :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request includes the descendants settled there and people joining them; unlike 2:126 it is not restricted to believers because prayer has already been named.
rows.anchor: وارزقهم أي ذريتي الذين أسكنتهم هناك أو مع من ينحاز إليهم من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fruit may come from nearby villages or distant lands; both happened, so spring, summer, and autumn fruits can gather in the sanctuary on one day.
rows.anchor: من الثمرات من أنواعها بأن يجعل بقرب منه قرى يحصل فيها ذلك أو يجبي إليه من الأقطار البعيدة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Ṭāʾif, three stages from Mecca and originally part of Palestine, was lifted and placed as provision for the sanctuary after Abraham prayed.
rows.anchor: روى عن ابن عباس أن الطائف وهي على ثلاث مراحل من مكة كانت من أرض فلسطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people should thank God for this provision through prayer and the other observances of servitude.
rows.anchor: لعلهم يشكرون تلك النعمة بإقامة الصلاة وأداء سائر مراسم العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī favors the view that Abraham prayed after the House was built and after arriving: the physical reference to the city and sacred House, and 14:39’s mention of Isaac, support that chronology.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : اختلف العلماء في أن هذا الدعاء بعد بناء البيت أو قبل أول ما قدم مكة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say this city refers to its mental conception before it existed, since God disclosed its location; the prayer asks hearts to settle with Abraham’s descendants, not merely visit the House for pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الإشارة في هذا البلد إلى الموجود في الذهن قبل تحقق البلدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī objects that the pronoun does not rule out pilgrimage: the wording may elide place, meaning hearts incline to their noble place for pilgrimage, as al-Taysīr explains.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : فيه نظر لأنه لم لا يجوز أن يكون المعنى على حذف المضاف

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshād explains calling it a House before construction by reference to its former location, then a raised mound whose floods flowed off to either side.
rows.anchor: قال في الإرشاد : تسميته إذ ذاك بيتا ولم يكن له بناء وإنما كان نشزا

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Bursevī says the Kaaba’s repeated rebuilding is certain, while scholars differ over how many times it was rebuilt, citing al-Kāshifī.
rows.anchor: وإنما الاختلاف في كمية عدده ، كما قال الكاشفي عند

words: إِنَّكَ تَعْلَمُ مَا نُخْفِى وَمَا نُعْلِنُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham discloses needs not to inform God, who already knows them, but to display servitude and need for mercy and hasten divine gifts.
rows.anchor: مقصده إن إظهار هذه الحاجات ليس لكونها غير معلومة لك

words: وَمَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing is hidden from God at any time; past, present, and future do not apply to Him, and His essential knowledge relates equally to all known things, unlike acquired human or angelic knowledge.
rows.anchor: وما يخفي دائما إذ لا ماضي ولا مستقبل ولا حال بالنسبة إلى الله تعالى

words: مِن شَىْءٍۢ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is exhaustive; the phrase says no thing in earth or heaven escapes God, so He should do what benefits them.
rows.anchor: من للاستغراق شيء ما في الأرض ولا في السماء لأنه العالم بعلم ذاتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the earth and heaven may modify is hidden or describe a thing located there.
rows.anchor: فالظرف متعلق بيخفى أو شيء ما كائن فيهما على أنه صفة لشيء

words: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِى وَهَبَ لِى عَلَى الْكِبَرِ إِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ʿalā means with and is circumstantial: God gave Abraham children when old and despairing of them; he stresses old age to magnify the blessing at an infertile time.
rows.anchor: على ههنا معنى مع وهو في موقع الحال أي وهب لي وأنا كبير آيس من الولد

rows.speaker: معالم التنزيل
rows.claim: Maʿālim al-Tanzīl explains Ishmael’s name by Abraham’s plea for a child, Hear, O El; Ishmael was born when Abraham was ninety-nine.
rows.anchor: إسماعيل سمى إسماعيل لأن إبراهيم كان يدعو الله أن يرزقه ولدا

rows.speaker: إنسان العيون
rows.claim: Insān al-ʿUyūn gives Ishmael’s Hebrew meaning as obedient to God and Isaac’s as laughing; Isaac was born when Abraham was 112 and Ishmael thirteen.
rows.anchor: وقال في إنسان العيون معناه بالعبرانية مطيع الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is responsive to prayer, as a king is said to hear someone when taking their words into account.
rows.anchor: أي : لمجيبه من قولهم سمع الملك كلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase implies Abraham prayed for a child, as in 37:100; God answered when he had despaired, making the gift especially great.
rows.anchor: فأجابه ووهب له سؤله حين ما وقع اليأس منه ليكون من أجل النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqīm may mean straightening prayer, keeping it flourishing like a market, or performing it.
rows.anchor: معدلا لها من أقمت العود إذا قومته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The active participle rather than a verb meaning I establish signals continuity and persistence.
rows.anchor: والاستمرار يستفاد من العدول من الفعل إلى الاسم حيث لم يقل اجعلني أقيم الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From my descendants means some of them, since Abraham knew unbelievers would occur among descendants; this qualifies the lasting word in his progeny (43:28).
rows.anchor: ومن ذريتي أي وبعض ذريتي عطف على المنصوب في اجعلني وإنما بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishārī, establishing prayer signifies continuing ascent, since prayer is the believer’s miʿrāj, an enduring journey in and through God.
rows.anchor: والإشارة إلى إقامة الصلاة إلى إدامة العروج فإن الصلاة معراج المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks God to accept his prayer that he and some descendants establish prayer, remain firm in it, and avoid idol worship; he uses the plural because the request includes them.
rows.anchor: وجعل بعض ذريتي مقيمي الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request covers leaving what was best in religion and other human shortcomings; Abraham prayed for his parents before their situation became clear.
rows.anchor: مافرط مني من ترك الأولى في باب الدين وغير ذلك مما لا يسلم منه البشر

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: Al-Kawāshī says Abraham sought forgiveness while his parents lived, hoping they would be guided, or because his mother became Muslim and he hoped his father would follow; some read my mother.
rows.anchor: في الكواشي : استغفر لأبويه وهما حيان طمعا في هدايتهما

rows.speaker: السيوطي
rows.claim: Al-Suyūṭī infers that Abraham’s Quranic father was his uncle, not biological father: the unbelieving father in 9:114 is the one Abraham disavowed, and Arabs called an uncle father.
rows.anchor: وقال الحافظ السيوطي يستنبط من قول إبراهيم.

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith says Abraham meets Āzar at Resurrection, hears his renewed promise not to disobey, pleads against the shame of his father in Hell, and is shown a transformed creature taken to the Fire.
rows.anchor: قال في "حياة الحيوان" : في الحديث : يلقى إبراهيم أباه آزر يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āzar becomes a shaggy male hyena because its proverbial foolishness mirrors his failure to heed Abraham and trust in Satan; God avoids a dog or pig form to spare Abraham’s honor.
rows.anchor: والحكمة في كونه مسخ ضبعا دون غيره من الحيوان أن الضبع لما كان يغفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A couplet illustrates the warning: while the oppressed is awake praying against the oppressor, God’s eye never sleeps.
rows.anchor: نامت عيونك والمظلوم منتبه يدعو عليك وعين الله لم تنم

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdī’s Persian verses warn oppressors to fear the wronged person’s sigh and dawn prayer and the burning pain of a night of grief.
rows.anchor: قال السعدي قدس سره :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishārī, God was never unaware in eternity of present oppressors’ deeds; all occur by His decree and wisdom, with happiness or misery embedded in deeds and lifespans, so He delays wrongdoers to increase sin and lead them to the abode of the wretched.
rows.anchor: ولا تحسبن الله غافلا أي في الأزل عما يعمل الظالمون اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is to warn all people.
rows.anchor: أي خوفهم جميعا يا محمد يوم يأتيهم العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day of punishment may mean the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي من يوم القيامة أو من يوم موتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively it may mean the day they die, since death is the first punishment and its agonies begin then.
rows.anchor: فإنه أول أيام عذابهم حيث يعذبون بالسكرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning primarily addresses unbelievers and secondarily believers, though believers will not be punished.
rows.anchor: وهذا الإنذار للكفرة أصالة وللمؤمنين تبعية وإن لم يكونوا معذبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who wronged themselves are the people among them who committed shirk and denied the truth.
rows.anchor: فيقول الذين ظلموا منهم بالشرك والتكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask to be returned to worldly life and granted respite.
rows.anchor: ربنا أخرنا ردنا إلى الدنيا وأمهلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A near term means a short span or limit of time.
rows.anchor: إلى أجل قريب إلى أمد وحد من الزمان قريب

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Saʿdī al-Muftī suggests an ellipsis: return us to the possessor of a near term, meaning the world, while delaying punishment.
rows.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي لعل في النظم تضمينا

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī paraphrases the plea as postponing punishment, returning them to the world, and giving a short respite.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (عذاب مارا تأخيركن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask to stay alive long enough to believe and answer God’s call to Him and His oneness.
rows.anchor: وأبقنا مقدار ما نؤمن بك ونجيب دعوتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They promise to follow the messengers’ teachings and make up for neglecting the call and messengers.
rows.anchor: ونتبع الرسل فيما جاؤنا به

words: أَوَلَمْ تَكُونُوا۟ أَقْسَمْتُم مِّن قَبْلُ مَا لَكُم مِّن زَوَالٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are reproached: had they not been given time in worldly life and sworn arrogantly that they would never leave it?
rows.anchor: على إضمار القول عطفا على فيقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels in their original form are seen when they descend to bring punishment or at death; when sent in that form they give no respite and torment follows immediately.
rows.anchor: يعني ملك رابصورت أصلي وقتى توانند ديدكه بجهت عذاب نازل شوند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic نحن magnifies God’s majesty and exalted rank.
rows.anchor: لعظم شأننا وعلو جنابنا ونحن

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: Al-Kawāshī says نحن is not a separator because it stands between two nouns; it is instead a subject.
rows.anchor: ونحن ليست بفصل لأنها بين اسمين وإنما هي مبتدأ كما في الكواشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Reminder is the Book deniers rejected and whose revelation to Muhammad they denied; they accused him of madness and obscured its Revealer by using the passive form.
rows.anchor: ذلك الذكر الذي أنكروه وأنكروا نزوله عليك ونسبوك بذلك إلى الجنون

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī says dhikr can mean honor: the Book brings honor and glory in this world and the next, as in 23:71.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (وذكر بمعنى شرف نيز مى آيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God preserves the Quran from attacks, denial, mockery, distortion, alteration, addition, and deletion.
rows.anchor: كالطعن فيه والمجادلة في حقيته والتكذيب له والاستهزاء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier scriptures developed errors because God did not undertake to preserve them and entrusted their keeping to people.
rows.anchor: وأما الكتب المتقدمة فلما لم يتول حفظها واستحفظها الناس تطرق إليها الخلل

rows.speaker: التبيان
rows.claim: Al-Tibyān says God guards the Quran against devils’ whispers and mixtures, preventing false additions and deletion of truth.
rows.anchor: وفي التبيان أو حافظون له من الشياطين من وساوسهم

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Baḥr al-ʿUlūm explains preservation as ṣarfah: people could alter or diminish the Quran as earlier scriptures, but God turned them away from it.
rows.anchor: في بحر العلوم : حفظه إياه بالصرفة على معنى أن الناس كانوا قادرين

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: He also explains preservation through scholars and their works on the Quran’s wording and meanings, including tafsir and readings.
rows.anchor: أو بحفظ العلماء وتصنيفهم الكتب التي صنفوها في شرح الفاظه ومعانيه

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The Mathnawī says God promised the Quranic lesson would not die with Muhammad and guards the miraculous Book from increase and decrease.
rows.anchor:
في المثنوى :
مصطفى را وعده كرد الطاف حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outwardly, God shaped Adam in human form; the breath means air entering a body able to retain it and is metaphor for creating life.
rows.anchor: أي صورته بالصورة الإنسانية والخلقة البشرية ونفخت فيه من روحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no literal breath or breathed substance: the phrase describes the Creator’s relation to the created and manifestation of His attribute and act in Adam.
rows.anchor: ولا نفخ ثمة ولا منفوخ بل ليس عند الحقيقة

rows.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين
rows.claim: Shaykh ʿIzz al-Dīn says breath signifies ignition of the soul’s light in a receptive place; the physical image cannot apply to God, but its effect can be named for its cause.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ عز الدين : النفخ عبارة عما اشعل نور الروح

rows.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين
rows.claim: For ʿIzz al-Dīn, the active cause is divine generosity, spring of existence and power, while the receiver is the balance created by shaping.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ عز الدين : النفخ عبارة عما اشعل

rows.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين
rows.claim: He likens the receptive quality to a polished mirror that takes the image facing it; the soul appears when the embryo reaches balance.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ عز الدين : النفخ عبارة عما اشعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian couplet compares the heart to a polished mirror capable of receiving limitless forms, and says polishers immediately see beauty.
rows.anchor: آن صفاي آينه وصفت دلست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God adds the breath to Himself because He personally shaped Adam with His holy hands and breathed directly, without intermediary.
rows.anchor: وإنما أضاف النفخ إلى ذاته لأنه تعالى باشر تسويته وتعديله فخلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attributed spirit is the breath of the All-Merciful and shadowy existence, linked to 25:45.
rows.anchor: من روحه الإضافي وهو نفسه الرحماني الذي يقال له الوجود الظلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This direct divine breath into Adam’s shaped form entails knowledge of all the Names, both gracious and majestic.
rows.anchor: نفخا استلزم لكونه نفخا بالذات فيما بوشرت تسويته باليدين معرفة الأسماء كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faqaʿū is the imperative of waqaʿa and requires falling prostrate, not merely bowing, in obedience and as honor for Adam, who displays divine wonders like a qibla.
rows.anchor: أمر من وقع يقع وفيه دليل على أنه ليس المأمور به مجرد الانحناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī recounts a true dream of his shaykh: he remained pure to his last breath, then performed ablution at a spring after death, ascended to heaven, and returned to pray at his own funeral.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : لي رؤيا صادقة في هذا المقام وهي أني رأيت حضرة شيخي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the dream, the shaykh answers that earthly intellect and perception remain after death.
rows.anchor: فقلت له هل يبقى العقل والإدراك الذي في هذه النشأة الدنيوية على حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī infers that ablution is invalidated at death agony, grounding the sounder view that a deceased person must be washed; the complete believer remains pure, since hadath is not impurity.
rows.anchor: منها أن الوضوء ينتقض عند النزع وعليه بني مشروعية الغسل في الأصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The complete person is washed as an imperfect person because outwardly he lacks ablution and follows the imperfect in worldly appearances.
rows.anchor: لأنه على غير وضوء بحسب الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intellect, faith, sainthood, and similar qualities belong to the spirit and therefore do not change at death.
rows.anchor: لأن العقل والإيمان والولاية ونحوها من صفات الروح وهو لا يتغير بالموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The perfected spirit’s funeral prayer signifies that in reality the perfected person is both prostrating and prostrated to; people’s prayer echoes angels’ prostration to Adam while remaining supplication at the legal level.
rows.anchor: فصلاته على نفسه إشارة إلى أن الكامل هو الساجد والمسجود له في مرتبة الحقيقة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya reads shaping as making Adam fit to receive the divine breath; the possessive spirit marks its special nearness and rank in the highest heavenly realm (50:16).
rows.anchor: قال في التأويلات النجمية : فإذا سويته تسوية تجعله قابلا لنفختي

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The spirit descends through angels, whose luminous qualities fold into it like starlight into sunlight; it then passes through jinn and devils, taking their traits, and through animals, receiving senses and powers.
rows.anchor: لأن الروح لما أرسل من أعلى مراتب القرب بنفخة الحق تعالى إلى أسفل سافلين

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The spirit attaches to Adam’s form, molded by God with gentleness and severity and prepared for manifestation; God commands prostration because of Adam’s perfected form, knowledge, and capacity for disclosure.
rows.anchor: ثم تعلق بالقالب المخلوق بيد الله المخمر فيه لطف الله وقهره المستعد لقبول التجلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those invoked are the gods worshipped by unbelievers; in Quranic usage, calling upon a deity often means worshipping it.
rows.anchor: أي : والآلهة الذين يعبدهم الكفار والدعاء بمعنى العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min dūni Allāh is circumstantial and means going beyond God; dūn first means a lower place, then difference in rank and broadly crossing a boundary or rule.
rows.anchor: نصب على الحال أي : متجاوزين الله فإن معنى دون أدنى مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols create nothing because creation is not within their capacity and they are powerless.
rows.anchor: أي : ليس من شأنهم ذلك لأنهم عجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Createdness is intrinsic to the idols, since contingent beings depend on a creator for their essence and existence.
rows.anchor: أي : شأنهم ومقتضى ذاتهم المخلوقية لأنها ذوات ممكنة مفتقرة

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs defines the Creator as the one who originates and invents a thing without a prior model.
rows.anchor: قال في "القاموس" : الخالق في صفاته المبدع للشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amwāt is the second predicate of the relative pronoun and plural of mayyit; the idols are lifeless objects though shaped like beings with souls.
rows.anchor: جمع ميت خبر ثان للموصول أي : جمادات لا حياة فيها

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs says mawāt can mean something without a soul or ownerless land.
rows.anchor: قال في "القاموس" : الموات كغراب وكسحاب ما لا روح فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayr aḥyāʾ means not capable of life, like sperm or an egg, and thus completely dead.
rows.anchor: جمع حي ضد الميت أي : غير قابلين للحياة كالنطفة والبيضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿūr means knowing, perceiving, or understanding something.
rows.anchor: الشعور (بدانستن) يقال : شعر به كنصر وكرم شعرا وشعورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayyān combines interrogative ay and time, so means when; unlike ayn, which asks where, it asks about time and is indeclinable on fatḥ like Baalbek.
rows.anchor: وأيان مركب من أي : التي للاستفهام وآن بمعنى الزمان فلذلك كان بمعنى متى

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs defines raising the dead as reviving them.
rows.anchor: وبعث الموتى نشرهم أي : إحياؤهم كما في "القاموس"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gods do not know when their worshippers will be raised; knowledge of resurrection’s timing is necessary to divinity, exposing idols’ deadness and inability to know their fate.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ما يعلم أولئك الآلهة متى يبعث عبدتهم من القبور
